zoombini: cannonlake: Add 5V power good signal. The 5V power good signal is being removed from the PMIC power good tree, however, if the 5V power good is not asserted, we should not try booting to S0. This is because the 1050_STG rail load switch is powered off of the 5V rail. Since wireless power control is being moved to the AP, these pins are now repurposed to control the PMIC enable and for the 5V power good signal. This commit adds the 5V power good pin to the EC and makes it a required power signal for S0. BUG=b:66000679 BRANCH=None TEST=make -j buildall TEST=flash zoombini; Verify EC boots up okay. lakitu: make systemd use the legacy cgroup hierarchy by default On newer kernel (ex: 4.12) systemd tries to use cgroup-v2 hierarchy for the systemd controller (this is the "hybrid" mode for systemd). It is unclear if this is useful for us right now or if this will lead to any issues. For now, to avoid unintended regression, force systemd to use the legacy cgroup hierarchy for everything which is the default behavior on current 4.4 kernel. This is achieved by setting: systemd.unified_cgroup_hierarchy=false systemd.legacy_systemd_cgroup_controller=true on the kernel command-line. See https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/systemd.html for details. This change is a no-op with the current 4.4 kernel. BUG=b:68010453 TEST=cloud_ProcessTree test fails because of this mismatch on newer kernel. With this patch, it passes. Also manually verified that legacy hierarchy is used. # Without this patch on 4.12 kernel (note the "cgroup2" fstype): $ cat /proc/mounts | grep "cgroup/systemd" tmpfs /sys/fs/cgroup tmpfs ro,nosuid,nodev,noexec,mode=755 0 0 cgroup /sys/fs/cgroup/systemd cgroup2 rw,nosuid,nodev,noexec,relatime 0 0 # With this patch on 4.12 kernel: $ cat /proc/mounts | grep "cgroup/systemd" cgroup /sys/fs/cgroup/systemd cgroup rw,nosuid,nodev,noexec,relatime,xattr,release_agent=/usr/lib/systemd/systemd-cgroups-agent,name=systemd 0 0 RELEASE_NOTE=None Change-Id: I00e45dd7fa3d72bb0499bed421e3e003804945c1 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/735979 Commit-Ready: Aditya Kali <adityakali@google.com> Tested-by: Aditya Kali <adityakali@google.com> Reviewed-by: Edward Jee <edjee@google.com> Reviewed-by: Daniel Wang <wonderfly@google.com>

CHROMIUM: wpa_supplicant: Full-scan after blacklisting wpa_supplicant currently blacklists APs that deauth it, and restricts the next scan to frequencies it has seen in prior scans of the ESS it was just connected to. This precludes APs that have changed frequencies from being discovered on subsequent scans. See CL:421224 for more details. This change adds a config to disable the scan restriction to previously seen frequencies.
